items.quote: Yet Ptolemy's *physical hypothesis*, that the Earth sat immobile at the center of the universe while planets moved on nested crystalline spheres and secondary circles pinned to primary circles, was erroneous. When **Nicolaus Copernicus** proposed placing the Sun at the center, and **Johannes Kepler**, working from **Tycho Brahe's** painstaking naked-eye measurements of Mars, discovered his three laws of planetary motion, Kepler matched the observations with far greater accuracy and without the artificial apparatus of epicycles. Those laws state that planets move in ellipses with the Sun at one focus, sweep out equal areas in equal times, and obey a precise mathematical ratio between orbital period and distance. That first transition demonstrates that **accurate numerical output within a limited dataset does not automatically validate the underlying physical explanation; when a simpler, more comprehensive model corresponds to reality more accurately, the earlier explanation must yield.**

Instead, living well is a **directed effort** measured by the positive rate of improvement between Time A and Time B.

items.quote: During the First Five-Year Plan (1928 to 1932), the Soviet Union bypassed individual entrance examinations in technical institutes to fill engineering seats by class quotas and graded students collectively in brigades; when graduates proved unable to keep industrial plants running, the Central Executive Committee issued its decree of September 19, 1932 abolishing collective grading and restoring individual examinations and theses. China repeated the experiment during the Cultural Revolution, abolishing the national university entrance examination (*gaokao*) in 1966 in favor of class-background recommendations; eleven years of crippled technical training forced Deng Xiaoping to restore the examination in 1977, stating that examinations check students' work just as the testing of factory products checks industrial quality.
